info.text: Unit 28 — Simulation: unscheduled defect escalation. Listening, reading, use of English (mixed conditionals), and vocabulary.

name.text: U28-L1 Dialogue 1 · what Deniss does first

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again (Finding the snag). After Marta reports the snag, what does Deniss decide to do to get more information?

generalfeedback.text: Deniss says he will run a BITE test on the hydraulic panel and download the fault codes. BITE (built-in test equipment) is the self-test that reads fault codes, so it is the natural first troubleshooting step.

answer.text: He runs a BITE test and reads the fault codes.

feedback.text: Correct. The BITE self-test gives him the two fault codes to work from.

answer.text: He signs the aircraft off and releases it for the flight.

feedback.text: No. Nobody can sign off until the fault is fixed and tested.

answer.text: He orders a brand-new pump straight from the main base.

feedback.text: No. The part is ordered much later, after the fault is confirmed.

answer.text: He tells Marta to postpone the whole check until the morning.

feedback.text: No. The team acts at once because the flight is at 06:00.

name.text: U28-L2 Dialogue 1 · the two fault codes

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. The BITE test returns two separate codes. What do the two codes point to?

generalfeedback.text: Deniss says one code indicates the pressure transducer and the other the pump. Because there are two possible causes, the team cannot yet confirm the root cause — that is why they open the AMM.

answer.text: The pressure transducer and the pump.

feedback.text: Correct. One sensor code and one pump code, so the cause is still uncertain.

answer.text: The landing gear and the cabin pressure controller.

feedback.text: No. Those systems are not mentioned in the dialogue at all.

answer.text: The main battery and the standby flight instruments.

feedback.text: No. The fault is in the green hydraulic system, not electrical power.

answer.text: The cargo door and the anti-ice valve on the wing.

feedback.text: No. Neither of these is part of the reported snag.

name.text: U28-L3 Dialogue 2 · defer under the MEL

questiontext.text:
Listen to Dialogue 2 again (Escalating to the supervisor). Decide if this sentence is true or false:

"Deniss says the green system pump can be deferred under the MEL, so the aircraft may still fly."

generalfeedback.text: False. Deniss reviewed the MEL and reports that the green system pump is a no-go item. A no-go item cannot be deferred, so the aircraft stays AOG until the pump is replaced.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Incorrect. It is a no-go item, so it cannot be deferred.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Correct. The pump is a no-go item and the defect cannot be deferred.

name.text: U28-L4 Dialogue 2 · workaround

questiontext.text:
Listen to Dialogue 2 again. Decide if this sentence is true or false:

"There is no safe workaround for the failed pump, and the team will not bend the regulations."

generalfeedback.text: True. Deniss says clearly that no safe workaround exists for a failed pump and that they never bend the regulations. This is why the case must be escalated.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct. No safe workaround, and no bending of the rules.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Incorrect. Deniss states there is no safe workaround.

name.text: U28-L5 Dialogue 1 · number of fault codes

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. How many separate fault codes does the BITE test return? Write the number as a figure.

generalfeedback.text: The BITE returns 2 separate codes — one for the pressure transducer and one for the pump. Hearing exact figures in speech is a real listening skill.

feedback.text: Correct — two codes.
Listen again: Deniss says the BITE returns two separate codes.

name.text: U28-L6 Dialogue 3 · total downtime

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again (Briefing the duty manager). About how many hours of total downtime does Ivan estimate (arrival plus install and test)? Write the number as a figure.

generalfeedback.text: Ivan says roughly six hours to arrive, then two hours to install and test — around eight hours of downtime in total. That is why the first rotation is lost.

feedback.text: Correct — about eight hours (six + two).
Six hours to arrive plus two hours to fit and test is about eight.

name.text: U28-L7 Voicemail · lead time in hours

questiontext.text: Listen to the Maintenance Control voicemail again. Approximately how many hours is the lead time for the replacement pump? Write the number as a figure.

generalfeedback.text: Maintenance Control says the lead time is approximately 6 hours by road. Lead time is the time to get a part after you order it.

feedback.text: Correct — about six hours.
The voicemail says approximately six hours by road.

name.text: U28-R1 Service Bulletin · action

questiontext.text:
Read this Service Bulletin extract, then answer.

SERVICE BULLETIN SB-29-0142
ATA 29 Hydraulic Power. Subject: Engine-Driven Pump (EDP) seal, improved design.
Reason: Field reports of internal leakage at the EDP shaft seal.
Compliance: Recommended at next pump removal. Not mandatory.
Action: Replace the old seal with the improved seal, part shown in the IPC.

According to this bulletin, when should operators carry out the action?

generalfeedback.text: The bulletin lists compliance as "recommended at next pump removal" and "not mandatory". A Service Bulletin (SB) is advice from the manufacturer; unlike an Airworthiness Directive (AD), it does not force immediate action.

answer.text: At the next pump removal; it is recommended, not mandatory.

feedback.text: Correct. An SB is recommended action, done at a convenient point.

answer.text: Immediately and by law, because every bulletin is compulsory.

feedback.text: No. An SB is not mandatory; an AD would be compulsory.

answer.text: Only after the aircraft has been fully painted and weighed.

feedback.text: No. Painting and weighing are unrelated to this bulletin.

answer.text: Never, because the bulletin has already been cancelled today.

feedback.text: No. The bulletin is active and recommends the seal change.

name.text: U28-R2 Work order · part source

questiontext.text:
Read this work order line, then answer.

WORK ORDER 4471-A
Task: Remove and replace green system EDP.
Part No: 29-4471-EDP (from IPC fig. 29-11-41).
Stores: NIL on station — nearest unit at main base.
Status: AOG. Transport requested.

Where did the technician get the part number on this work order?

generalfeedback.text: The line reads "from IPC fig. 29-11-41". The IPC (Illustrated Parts Catalogue) is where you look up the correct part number before ordering a spare.

answer.text: From the IPC (Illustrated Parts Catalogue).

feedback.text: Correct. The IPC gives the part number for the order.

answer.text: From the flight crew's spoken report on the radio.

feedback.text: No. The crew reports the snag, not the part number.

answer.text: From the weather briefing printed for the morning flight.

feedback.text: No. The weather briefing has nothing to do with parts.

answer.text: From the passenger manifest kept by the boarding gate.

feedback.text: No. The manifest lists passengers, not aircraft parts.

name.text: U28-R3 MEL entry · meaning

questiontext.text:
Read this simplified MEL entry, then answer.

MEL 29-10 Green System Engine-Driven Pump
Number installed: 1. Number required for dispatch: 1.
Remarks: No relief. Dispatch not allowed with this pump inoperative.

What does "Number required for dispatch: 1" tell the technician?

generalfeedback.text: One pump is installed and one is required to fly, with "no relief". So if that single pump fails, the aircraft cannot be dispatched — it is a no-go item and cannot be deferred.

answer.text: The pump must work for the flight; it is a no-go item.

feedback.text: Correct. Required for dispatch with no relief means no-go.

answer.text: The aircraft may fly for three more days with it failed.

feedback.text: No. "No relief" means there is no deferral period at all.

answer.text: One spare pump is always kept ready inside the cockpit.

feedback.text: No. The entry is about dispatch, not spares storage.

answer.text: The crew may choose to fly without the pump if in a hurry.

feedback.text: No. The crew cannot overrule a no-go MEL item.

name.text: U28-R4 Airworthiness Directive · mandatory

questiontext.text:
Read this Airworthiness Directive extract, then decide true or false.

AD 2026-15-03 — Applicable to all A320 series.
Required action: Inspect the EDP mounting bolts within 100 flight hours. Compliance is mandatory.

"An Airworthiness Directive (AD) is optional advice that operators may ignore."

generalfeedback.text: False. An AD is a mandatory instruction from the regulator; compliance is required by law. This is the key difference from a Service Bulletin, which is only recommended.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Incorrect. An AD is mandatory, not optional.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Correct. An AD must be complied with; it is not optional.

name.text: U28-R5 Tech log · sign-off status

questiontext.text:
Read this tech log line, then decide true or false.

Defect: Green EDP internal leak. Status: AOG, part ordered. Sign-off: pending.

"Because the sign-off is pending, the aircraft has not yet been released to service."

generalfeedback.text: True. "Sign-off: pending" means the certifying signature has not been given, so the aircraft is not yet returned to service. Sign-off is the last step before release.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct. Pending sign-off means no release yet.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Incorrect. Without sign-off the aircraft cannot be released.

name.text: U28-U1 Mixed conditional · past to now

questiontext.text:
Complete the mixed conditional. Write the two missing verb forms, separated by a comma.

"If we ______ (order) the spare last week, we ______ (have) it on the shelf now."

Example of the format to type: had ordered, would have

generalfeedback.text: The condition is in the past (we did not order), and the result is now (no spare today): had ordered, would have. Never use "would" in the if-clause.

answer.text: had ordered, would have

feedback.text: Correct — past condition, present result.

answer.text: had ordered would have

feedback.text: Correct — past condition, present result.
Use "had ordered" in the if-clause and "would have" for the present result.

name.text: U28-U2 Mixed conditional · now to past

questiontext.text:
Complete the mixed conditional. Write the two missing verb forms, separated by a comma.

"If this pump ______ (be) not a no-go item, we ______ (defer) it already."

Example of the format to type: were, would have deferred

generalfeedback.text: The condition is a state that is true now (it IS a no-go item), and the result is in the past (we did not defer): were, would have deferred. Use "were" for every person in this pattern.

answer.text: were, would have deferred

feedback.text: Correct — present state, past result.

answer.text: were would have deferred

feedback.text: Correct — present state, past result.
Use "were" (not "was") and "would have deferred" for the past result.

name.text: U28-U3 Correct the if-clause error

questiontext.text:
Correct the grammar. Rewrite the if-clause correctly (only the two words that replace "would have ordered").

Wrong: "If we would have ordered the part, we would have it now."

Type the two correct words that replace "would have ordered".

generalfeedback.text: English never puts "would" in the if-clause. The past condition uses had ordered. This "would in both halves" habit comes from Latvian and Russian.

answer.text: had ordered

feedback.text: Correct. "If we had ordered the part..."
Use "had ordered" — no "would" in the if-clause.

name.text: U28-U4 Bank term · grounded and waiting

questiontext.text:
Write the correct bank term.

The three-letter term for an aircraft that is grounded and waiting for an urgent part is ______.

generalfeedback.text: AOG means "aircraft on ground": grounded and waiting for urgent parts. You say "declare AOG".

answer.text: AOG

feedback.text: Correct — aircraft on ground.

answer.text: an AOG

feedback.text: Correct — aircraft on ground.
The term is AOG (aircraft on ground).

name.text: U28-U5 Bank term · pass it up the chain

questiontext.text:
Write the correct bank term (one verb).

When stores has no spare and you cannot fix the fault at your level, you must ______ the problem to Maintenance Control.

generalfeedback.text: To escalate is to pass a problem up to a higher level for a decision. The noun is "escalation".

answer.text: escalate

feedback.text: Correct — escalate to a higher level.
The verb is "escalate".

name.text: U28-U6 Bank term · temporary way to keep going

questiontext.text:
Write the correct bank term (one word).

A temporary way to keep going without a full repair is called a ______. For a failed pump, no safe one exists.

generalfeedback.text: A workaround is a temporary way to keep going without a full repair. In this unit there is no safe workaround for a failed pump.

answer.text: workaround

feedback.text: Correct — a temporary way round the problem.

answer.text: a workaround

feedback.text: Correct — a temporary way round the problem.
The word is "workaround".

name.text: U28-V1 Match term to meaning

questiontext.text: Match each term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: These five terms are the core escalation vocabulary: showstopper, MEL, snag, root cause, sign-off.

answer.text: a problem that stops all work until it is fixed
the legal list of what may be inoperative
an informal word for a fault or defect
the real, underlying reason for a fault
the certifying signature that releases the work
the time to get a part after you order it

name.text: U28-V2 Match document to its use

questiontext.text: Match each maintenance document to what you use it for.

generalfeedback.text: AMM = repair procedures; IPC = part numbers; tech log = running defect record; BITE = self-test fault codes.

answer.text: the official step-by-step repair procedures
where you find the correct part number
the aircraft's running record of defects
a self-test that gives fault codes
a passenger boarding document

name.text: U28-V3 Collocation · recovery plan

questiontext.text: Choose the natural collocation. Which verb goes best with "a recovery plan"?

generalfeedback.text: We agree a recovery plan — the manager and the team settle on the plan together. "Agree a recovery plan" is the natural workplace collocation.

answer.text: We agree a recovery plan with the manager.

feedback.text: Correct. "Agree a recovery plan" is the natural collocation.

answer.text: We pour a recovery plan before the morning flight.

feedback.text: No. "Pour" collocates with liquids, not plans.

answer.text: We fasten a recovery plan onto the wing bolts.

feedback.text: No. "Fasten" is for physical parts, not a plan.

answer.text: We overhaul a recovery plan inside the hangar.

feedback.text: No. "Overhaul" is for components, not for plans.

name.text: U28-V4 Collocation · BITE test

questiontext.text: Choose the natural collocation. Which verb goes best with "a BITE test"?

generalfeedback.text: We run a BITE test — "run a test" is the standard collocation for a self-test that produces fault codes.

answer.text: run a BITE test on the hydraulic panel

feedback.text: Correct. "Run a BITE test" is the standard collocation.

answer.text: bake a BITE test on the hydraulic panel

feedback.text: No. "Bake" is for food, not for a self-test.

answer.text: harvest a BITE test on the hydraulic panel

feedback.text: No. "Harvest" collocates with crops, not tests.

answer.text: whistle a BITE test on the hydraulic panel

feedback.text: No. "Whistle" does not collocate with a test.
